6 KB.**\n* **A refresh token is optional, and usually best left out.** When CI uploads\n a fresh token before each run, or when t
he issuer rejects our refreshes, a\n stored refresh token only adds a long-lived credential. Without one, an\n expired account l
ists `needsReconnect: true` and keeps its id until the next\n upload restores it.\n* **Uploads are budgeted** per person and serv

er: 60, refilling at 120 an
 hour. Past it the answer is `429` with `Retry-After`.

### Who can upload

An API key acts as t
he person who created it, with all of that person's\naccess. For personal accounts, upload with the key of a dedicated member who\
nis not a project admin, so a leaked CI key can't do an admin's work. On a\nserver shared with the project, accounts are project a

ccounts: only a project
admin can upload, rename or delete them, and every member's hosted runs can
use them.

### Running eva

ls as an account

A run with no saved account choice acts as the server's **default** account.
To run evals from CI as one acco

unt, upload its token, make it the default,
then start the run:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -fsS -X PATC
H \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"Authorizat

ion: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{ "isDefault": true }'
```

The CLI takes
the same steps with `mcpjam cloud server-accounts set`, which\nreads the token from a file, an environment variable or stdin, and
\n`mcpjam cloud server-accounts default`. See the\n[CLI reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md#cloud-server-accounts-

commands).

The default is shared by every run that key starts, so don't run the same
key's runs at the same time with differen
t defaults. Where your organization\nhas account choice for eval suites, a suite can instead save the accounts it\nruns as, in its

settings in the app; a run with a saved choice uses those
accounts and ignores the default.

### Deleting an account

`DELET
E` removes the account and its stored token, and asks the token's issuer\nto revoke the token where the issuer supports revocation
. That is best effort,\nand it also ends any copy of the same token you still hold. The default\naccount can't be deleted while ot

her accounts exist (`409`): make another
account the default first.

### The deprecated import route

`POST .../oauth/import-
tokens` still works, and is removed 90 days after the\naccounts API shipped. It uploads to your default account, creating an unnam
ed\none when the server has none, and keeps its old body and its old\n`{ imported, expiresAt }` answer. Every answer carries `Depr

ecation: true`, a
`Sunset` date and a `Link` to `.../accounts`.

An account this route creates is hosted-only. An existing defa
ult it writes\ninto keeps whatever rule it had. Its `serverUrl` must be the URL saved in the\nproject, or the answer is `400`. `au
thorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourceUrl`\nand `tokens.id_token` are accepted and ignored. Move to\n`PUT .../accounts/{account}`,

which names the account it writes.

The error codes these routes add to `details.code` are listed in the
[error code reference]

(https://docs.mcpjam.com/troubleshooting/error-codes.md#server-account-errors).

## Run evals from the API

The shortest usefu
mmediately; -f + jq -e fail fast on errors)\nRUN_ID=$(curl -fsS -X POST \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID
/eval-runs\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n -d '{\n \"sui

teName": "smoke",
 "serverIds": ["'$SERVER_ID'"],
 "tests": [{
 "title": "echo works",
 "runs":

1,
 "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5",
 "provider": "anthropic",
 "steps": [
 { "id": \

"s1", "kind": "prompt", "prompt": "Use the echo tool to say hi" },
 {
 "id": "s2",
 "kin

d": "assert",
 "assertion": {
 "type": "toolCalledWith",
 "toolName": "echo",
until status is completed | failed | cancelled | timed_out\ncurl -s \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs

/$RUN_ID" \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY"

# 3. If it did not pass, read the decision summary FIRST
curl -s
\"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID/decision-summary\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJA

M_API_KEY"

# 4. Or go straight to per-iteration tool calls, token usage, latency
curl -s "https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/proj

ects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID/iterations" \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY"
```

The decision summary co
mposes steps 2 and 4 into one versioned object so every\nclient reads a run the same way. Four things to know before gating on it:

* **`measurementUnit` ships with every count.** Under per-case grading the
 counts are case-execution *variants*, with itera
tions as trials inside them;\n under a suite-wide accuracy threshold they are trials. The same suite reports\n a different total
under each — 3 against 15 for three cases run five times —\n so a count without its unit is not a fact, and a rate is never conv

erted
 across that line.
* **It explains the verdict; it never re-decides it.** The run's own decision is
 the authority and
is carried through on `decision`. The per-trial\n `diagnostics` sit underneath it — a case can pass with a failing trial in it,\n
so tallying diagnostics gives a different answer than the platform reached.\n* **`verdict: \"notEstablished\"` is not a failure
and not `inconclusive`.** It\n means no verdict exists at all (unfinished, stopped early, or undecidable);\n `undecided.reason`
says which. `inconclusive` *is* a decision — the validity\n phase ran and withheld a verdict.\n* **`diagnostics.complete` says wh
ether you have the whole list.** A page\n fetched with a `cursor` is never complete, and `scannedIterations` separates\n \"nothi

ng failed" from "we did not look".

Evidence is scoped to the claim it supports: for a measured failure the span
ids, prompt
indexes and reasons come from the first failed stage's row alone,\nand `evidence.tracePath` is an API-relative path you can appen

d to your base URL
to read the full trace.

`model` takes an id from the hosted catalog — `provider/name` form, e.g.
`anthropi
c/claude-haiku-4.5` — and runs on your organization's credits.\nProvider-native ids (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-5`) are bring-your-own-
key: pass\nthe key in `modelApiKeys`. A model the API can't execute is rejected at\ncreate time with `VALIDATION_ERROR`; `details.

hostedModels` lists the valid
hosted ids for that provider.

Reruns are even shorter: `{ "suiteId": "..." }` reruns the sui
te exactly as\nconfigured, connecting the suite's saved server selection (the `202` response\nlists the resolved `servers`). Pass
`serverIds` to override the selection; a\nsuite with no saved selection requires it (`VALIDATION_ERROR` with\n`details.reason: \"N

O_SAVED_SERVER_SELECTION"` otherwise).

### Running against a project environment

A [project environment](#endpoints) is lau
nchable only through a suite that has\nit **attached**. Attach them first with\n`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}
` and an `environmentIds`\narray (send `null` to detach them all; `[]` is rejected — use `null`), then\npass `environmentId` on th
e run. It must be one of that suite's attached\nenvironments; anything else is a `400` with\n`details.reason: \"ENVIRONMENT_NOT_AT

TACHED"`, raised before any case is
authored or any server connected.

Omitting `environmentId` is meaningful, and depends on
hat environment is used automatically. The `202`\n response's `environment` field says so;\n* **several** attached → `400` with `

details.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_REQUIRED"`,
 naming the candidates.
